readout_other: Intracellular current-clamp recordings from a motor axon and a muscle fiber of the crayfish opener neuromuscular preparation
direction_notes: FUS reliably produced hyperpolarization (FUSH) in motor axons at pressures of 0.1-0.6 MPa; FUSH was enhanced by cooling, unaffected by heating, not suppressed by K2P channel blockers, and largely absent in muscle fibers.

target.label: crayfish opener neuromuscular junction (motor axon and muscle fiber)

timing.protocol_description: An 80 ms burst of continuous sinusoidal waves at 2.1 MHz was used in temperature experiments. Optimal intensity per preparation (typically 0.3-0.6 MPa) was the level at which FUS-evoked depolarization occurred in <5% of trials; this was then used for the remainder of the experiment. A typical cycle included three trials (FUS alone, an AP train alone, FUS and an AP train simultaneously) with a 10 s rest between trials.

Thirty FUS tone bursts at 1 kHz with 50% duty cycle were delivered to trigger FUSH, chosen to visualize hyperpolarization evoked by individual bursts; each tone burst lasted 500 microseconds. A typical cycle contained eight current steps (four hyperpolarizing, four depolarizing) with a 2 s rest between steps, repeated with and without FUS, in the presence of fluoxetine, norfluoxetine, or Ba2+ to test K2P channel involvement.
